episodes.title: What Is Theater?
episodes.description: Explore definitions of theater and how people across different periods and cultures have understood performance.

episodes.title: Thespis, Athens, and The Origins of Greek Drama
episodes.description: The earliest recorded drama in the west arose in Athens, and these early plays grew out of religious rituals.

episodes.title: Tragedy Lessons from Aristotle
episodes.description: Explore Aristotle’s elements of tragedy and how theatrical suffering can produce catharsis for an audience.

episodes.title: Greek Comedy, Satyrs, and Aristophanes
episodes.description: Trace the development of ancient Greek comedy through satyr plays and later comic forms.

episodes.title: Dances to Flute Music and Obscene Verse. It’s Roman Theater, Everybody
episodes.description: Mike Rugnetta takes you from our beginnings in ancient Greek theater and moves on to the development of Roman theater.

episodes.title: Roman Theater with Plautus, Terence, and Seneca
episodes.description: In which Mike delves into the theater of ancient Rome.

episodes.title: Nostrils, Harmony with the Universe, and Ancient Sanskrit Theater
episodes.description: You'll learn about the drama of ancient India and its connection to the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.

episodes.title: The Death and Resurrection of Theater as…Liturgical Drama
episodes.description: Examine theater’s decline in the Christian West and its return through religious drama within the Catholic mass.

episodes.title: Hrotsvitha, Hildegard, and the Nun who Resurrected Theater
episodes.description: Explore Hrotsvitha’s moral comedies and her influence on later religious dramatists, including Hildegard of Bingen.

episodes.title: Get Outside and Have a (Mystery) Play
episodes.description: Today we'll learn about mystery plays, cycle plays, pageant wagons, and how medieval European theater moved from being a religious phenomenon to a secular one.

episodes.title: Just Say Noh. But Also Say Kyogen
episodes.description: Mike is taking you to Japan to have a look at Noh theater.

episodes.title: Pee Jokes, the Italian Renaissance, Commedia Dell’Arte
episodes.description: Explore Italian Renaissance theater amid the broader flourishing of art and humanism.

episodes.title: The English Renaissance and NOT Shakespeare
episodes.description: Explore Renaissance London’s theaters and the playwrights whose work preceded Shakespeare.

episodes.title: Straight Outta Stratford-Upon-Avon – Shakespeare’s Early Days
episodes.description: Explore Shakespeare’s early life, family, and entry into London’s theatrical world.

episodes.title: Shakespeare’s Tragedies and an Acting Lesson
episodes.description: Examine how Shakespeare changed tragedy through sympathetic protagonists such as Hamlet, Macbeth, and Lear.

episodes.title: Comedies, Romances, and Shakespeare’s Heroines
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Theater, Mike Rugnetta examines the comedies and romances of William Shakespeare.

episodes.title: English Theater After Shakespeare
episodes.description: Follow English theater after Shakespeare through Ben Jonson, revenge tragedy, court masques, and the threat of prohibition.

episodes.title: Where Did Theater Go?
episodes.description: Follow English theater through Puritan suppression, the Restoration, women’s arrival onstage, and Restoration comedy.

episodes.title: The Spanish Golden Age
episodes.description: Mike and Yorick take us to beautiful Spain and look at its Golden Age.

episodes.title: Rules, Rule-Breaking, and French Neoclassicism
episodes.description: Explore French neoclassical theatrical rules through Racine’s adherence and Corneille’s departures.

episodes.title: Moliere – Man of Satire and Many Burials
episodes.description: Mike Rugnetta teaches you about the greatest playwright of Renaissance France, Moliere.

episodes.title: Pre-Columbian Theater, Spanish Empire, and Sor Juana
episodes.description: Explore theater in the Americas before European arrival, Spanish colonial influence, and playwright Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz.

episodes.title: Japan, Kabuki, and Bunraku
episodes.description: Explore Edo-period Japanese performance through Kabuki’s dramatic action and Bunraku’s puppet theater.

episodes.title: All Night Demon Dance Party – Kathakali
episodes.description: We're headed to India to learn about the all-night dance shows that culminate in killing a Demon (metaphorically): Kathakali!

episodes.title: China, Zaju, and Beijing Opera
episodes.description: We're headed to China to learn about the ancient origins of theater there.

episodes.title: England’s Sentimental Theater
episodes.description: We're headed back to England to learn about Sentimental Comedies.

episodes.title: Why So Angry, German Theater?
episodes.description: Explore Sturm und Drang, Weimar Classicism, and Goethe’s Faust in German theater.

episodes.title: The Rise of Melodrama
episodes.description: Discover how theatrical licensing restrictions and musical entertainment helped shape melodrama.

episodes.title: North America Gets a Theater…Riot
episodes.description: Trace North American theater from Indigenous storytelling through European settlement, the Revolutionary era, and a notorious Macbeth-related riot.

episodes.title: Race Melodrama and Minstrel Shows
episodes.description: Examine how nineteenth-century American performance culture created and spread racist stereotypes. Includes discussion of disturbing images and language.

episodes.title: Zola, France, Realism, and Naturalism
episodes.description: We're back in Europe to learn about Realism and Naturalism.

episodes.title: Realism Gets Even More Real
episodes.description: Explore how staging, acting, sets, and rehearsal practices advanced theatrical realism across Europe.

episodes.title: Symbolism, Realism, and a Nordic Playwright Grudge Match
episodes.description: Explore Ibsen and Strindberg’s rivalry and their influence on modern European theater.

episodes.title: Chekhov and the Moscow Art Theater
episodes.description: Explore Russian theatrical modernism through Catherine the Great, Chekhov, the Moscow Art Theater, and Stanislavski’s acting theories.

episodes.title: The Horrors of the Grand Guignol
episodes.description: Explore the Grand Guignol’s violent stagecraft, special effects, and influence on later horror entertainment.

episodes.title: Synge, Wilde, Shaw, and the Irish Renaissance
episodes.description: The Irish Renaissance in the early 20th century included a wealth of new plays written both in Ireland and by Irish ex-patriots elsewhere.

episodes.title: Dada, Surrealism, and Symbolism
episodes.description: Trace the connections among Symbolism, Dada, and Surrealist theater through influential playwrights and productions.

episodes.title: Expressionist Theater
episodes.description: Explore expressionist theater’s dark response to mechanization, industrial society, and the pressures of modern life.

episodes.title: Futurism and Constructivism
episodes.description: Explore Italian Futurism and Meyerhold’s role in Russian theatrical constructivism.

episodes.title: Little Theater and American Avant Garde
episodes.description: Explore the Little Theater movement’s response to commercial melodrama and Eugene O’Neill’s groundbreaking plays.

episodes.title: The Harlem Renaissance
episodes.description: In the 1920s, there was a blossoming of all kinds of art made by African Americans in the New York neighborhood of Harlem.

episodes.title: Federal Theatre and Group Theater
episodes.description: Explore Depression-era American theater through the Federal Theatre Project and the influential Group Theatre.

episodes.title: Antonin Artaud and the Theater of Cruelty
episodes.description: The Theater of Cruelty was meant to force an audience into looking at the ridiculous illusions of their bourgeois lives.

episodes.title: Bertolt Brecht and Epic Theater
episodes.description: Learn how Brecht’s Epic Theater used performance to influence audiences and public opinion.

episodes.title: Beckett, Ionesco, and the Theater of the Absurd
episodes.description: Mike Rugnetta teaches you about the Theater of the Absurd, a 1950s theatrical reaction to the dire world events of the 1940s.

episodes.title: Broadway, Seriously
episodes.description: Explore social criticism on Broadway through Tennessee Williams, Arthur Miller, and Lorraine Hansberry.

episodes.title: The Birth of Off Broadway
episodes.description: Discover how Broadway’s commercial dominance helped create space for experimental work Off-Broadway.

episodes.title: Poor Unfortunate Theater
episodes.description: Poor Theater and Theater of the Oppressed were two sort of concurrent movements that shared some of the same aims.

episodes.title: Into Africa and Wole Soyinka
episodes.description: Today, we're going to talk about some of the dance and theater traditions of Africa, and look at post-colonial theater across the continent.

episodes.title: Broadway Book Musicals
episodes.description: Trace the development of book musicals from their early roots through Broadway’s Golden Age.
